A 16-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of a 1-month history of fever, headaches, and profound fatigue. Her temperature is 38.2°C (100.8°F). Examination shows splenomegaly. Laboratory studies show:
Leukocyte count 13,000/mm3 (15% atypical lymphocytes)
Serum
Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 60 U/L
Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 40 U/L
Heterophile antibody assay negative
EBV viral capsid antigen (VCA) antibodies negative
HIV antibody negative
In an immunocompromised host, the causal organism of this patient's symptoms would most likely cause which of the following conditions?"?

                    ### Question
                    A 16-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of a 1-month history of fever, headaches, and profound fatigue. Her temperature is 38.2°C (100.8°F). Examination shows splenomegaly. Laboratory studies show:
Leukocyte count 13,000/mm3 (15% atypical lymphocytes)
Serum
Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 60 U/L
Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 40 U/L
Heterophile antibody assay negative
EBV viral capsid antigen (VCA) antibodies negative
HIV antibody negative
In an immunocompromised host, the causal organism of this patient's symptoms would most likely cause which of the following conditions?"?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Multiple cerebral abscesses with surrounding edema
opb. Diffuse pulmonary infiltrates with pneumatoceles
opc. Purplish skin nodules on the distal extremities
opd. Non-scrapable white patches on the lateral tongue
ope. Linear ulcers near the lower esophageal sphincter

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings suggest a viral infection with atypical lymphocytes, negative heterophile antibody, and negative EBV VCA antibodies, pointing towards a Cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection. In an immunocompromised host, CMV is known to cause linear ulcers near the lower esophageal sphincter, which aligns with option 'ope'. The evidence paths related to atypical lymphocytes and viral infections support the consideration of CMV. Other options, such as diffuse pulmonary infiltrates with pneumatoceles, multiple cerebral abscesses, non-scrapable white patches on the lateral tongue, and purplish skin nodules, are more commonly associated with other infections or conditions in immunocompromised individuals, such as Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, bacterial or fungal infections, oral hairy leukoplakia (EBV), and Kaposi's sarcoma (HHV-8), respectively. Therefore, the most likely condition caused by CMV in an immunocompromised host is linear ulcers near the lower esophageal sphincter.
